name: How long does ground-up multifamily development take in Los Angeles from land closing to lease-up?

mainEntity.name: How long does a ground-up multifamily project usually take in Los Angeles once the site is secured?
mainEntity.text: How long does a ground-up multifamily project usually take in Los Angeles once the site is secured?

acceptedAnswer.text: A ground-up multifamily project in Los Angeles usually runs on a multi-year timeline. Smaller, straightforward infill projects may reach completion in about 24 to 30 months after site control, while larger or more complex developments can take 36 to 48 months or longer. The biggest schedule drivers are entitlement approval, plan check revisions, lender approval, demolition, shoring, utility upgrades, and construction type. After completion, lease-up can take another 3 to 12 months depending on unit mix, pricing, and neighborhood demand. Projects in Glendale, Pasadena, Burbank, and North Hollywood can also be slowed by zoning constraints, neighborhood review, and site-specific parking or access issues. A realistic schedule should include float for design changes, agency comments, weather delays, and material lead times. Anyone evaluating a project should ask for a milestone schedule with entitlement, permit, financing, construction, and lease-up phases separated clearly.
acceptedAnswer.description: A typical Los Angeles ground-up multifamily project can take roughly 24 to 48 months from site control to certificate of occupancy, depending on entitlements, plan check, financing, and construction type. Lease-up often adds several more months. In dense submarkets, permitting and utility coordination are usually the biggest schedule risks.
